assignment.name: Final Project Report (40%): due in Week13

rubric.long_description:
Background and contextual information related to this project



Overview of (1) project vision, (2) goals and objectives



Highlight and critically justify the project achievements and briefly explain how  to achieve the deliverables and fully meet all the project expectations (to match goals and vision)







Brief reflection on project management, client engagement, group dynamics and processes.

ratings.long_description:
The project introduction clearly explains and fully meets all the following criteria to a professional standard:
The background, overview of project vision, goals and objectives and other contextual information related to the project. Highlights the project achievements and briefly explain how to achieve the substantial achievements and expectations. Convincing contents demonstrating project completeness and highlights on the updates and progress since project progress report.

The project introduction properly explains and meets the substantial majority of the following criteria, OR meets all the criteria, but with some ambiguity, could be a refinement or improvement. Clear information demonstrating project completeness and highlights on some updates and progress since project progress report.

The project's introduction meets some of the criteria but misses out OR/AND not clearly addresses the following criteria. Basic information on project completeness and brief information on updates and progress since project progress report.

The project's introduction explains some basic criteria but misses out a major portion OR/AND there are flaws in the explanation of the criteria. Minimal information on project completeness and minimal information on updates and progress since project progress report.
The project introduction fails to explain and does not meet most of the criteria; or the contents are not relevant or primarily generated by AI.

rubric.long_description:
System Specifications



User stories and major project requirements- clear identification of functional and non-functional project and user requirements and accordingly design and define corresponding user stories.



Presentation of all the completed user stories designed based on specific functional or non-functional requirements



Each user story should be the smallest unit of work to satisfy specific functional or non-functional requirement.



Each user story should be clearly described and designed based on client's needs.



Each user story should be testable and estimable.



Identification of the functional and non-functional requirements expressed in each user story



Demonstration of user stories:



Detailed demonstration of implemented user stories within the final product and how they meet all the client requirements



Justify how well (quality) the most crucial user stories are implemented



It can include high-level designs (e.g., mock-ups, UIs)



List of user stories not completed/implemented/discarded/merged with justifications and rationale.







Other detailed documentation of



All aspects that were selected for the final product, including links to all relevant evidence for completion from GitHub (e.g. Relevant code, Jira issues);



Technical and other constraints (for example, reliability, security,...) regarding the use of algorithms, design patterns where applicable, and technology-related conditions or events that prevent the project from fully delivering the optimal solution to the client, customers or end-users.



Any other details that demonstrate the group went beyond the approved scope and the bare minimum.



Any other details that demonstrate the system specification and design that might be specific to the nature of the project (e.g., API integration, empirical evaluation of algorithms)



Summary and Highlights



Key changes requested by the client, and how these changes were handled or implemented as improvements/features.



Major improvements and Self-Reflections in contrast to the project progress report.







System Architecture and Design



Complete systems architecture and design (both text description and image illustration)



How you designed and implemented the system



High-level system component diagrams clearly articulate system components and their functionalities



Please justify the advantage of the system architecture and design



Main technical components of the system



Detailed explanation about how different components interact



Design patterns or off-the-shelf frameworks that you used along with relevant diagrams should also be described.



Clear statement of which components/parts are developed by the group, and which ones are adopted/utilized or need to integrate with.







Summary and Highlights



Key architecture and design changes requested by the client, and how these changes were handled or implemented.



Major improvements and Self-Reflections as comparison to the project progress report.

rubric.long_description:
Test strategy

Conducted with accompanying justification. (Justification on the sufficiency and the rationale of tests)

Not done and why (Justification on the non-rationality of tests)

Relevant testing techniques (e.g. Equivalence partitioning, boundary analysis)

Quality constraints consideration (e.g., security, performance, reliability, availability, etc)

The quality constraint focuses on the characteristics of the deliverable or product.

The quality of the project is evaluated by how closely the outcome matches the expectations set in the planning stages.

Other quality aspects or testing-related work specific to the project (e.g., API testing, UI testing, stress testing)

Test Demonstrate

Detailed Acceptance criteria and Acceptance tests are considered for each user story (for both functional and non-functional requirements) along with consideration for normal, boundary, and abnormal cases in each case

Test cases should be consistent with the corresponding user story and cover different aspects of all user stories

You can consider the format below or design your own format:

Demonstrate execution of designed test cases and corresponding results (e.g., bugs, bug fixes).

Demonstrate enough test coverage and explain why it is enough for the scope of the project

Summary of the significance and limitations of tests

rubric.description: Quality of Group Processes and Individual Contributions (20%)
rubric.long_description:
Summary of (up to one page for each member, otherwise all group members should agree on any changes) individual contributions, task splits and roles, corresponding extent, quality, and timeline (any delay) of completion of the allocated tasks should be included.

The group work and processes including:
the setup of tooling for development, management of tasks, allocation of tasks, the allocation of group roles (XP roles, technical responsibilities and non-technical tasks)

Evidence of collaboration and teamwork - group roles and sharing of work, group contract, meeting minutes (team, client, tutor), project status reports; and the use of GitHub, Teams, and other tools (as in the university recommendation list)

Critique - what has worked well and what needs to improve in terms of teamwork, group processes, and XP terms

rubric.description: Documentation Organization & Writing - GitHub Site & This Report (5%)
rubric.long_description:
The project report should follow a logical structure and adhere to professional standards and practices.
The individual contributions table should be included in the final report (as it is in template)
The structure of GitHub site and the documents (uploaded or directly written) should be well-organised and easy-to-read.
All the documentations should be well written in English and of a good quality, with no typos or grammatical errors.
The relevance between the evidence and the corresponding claim should be clear and obvious and the evidence should be clear and valid.
It should be easy for readers to find the corresponding evidence.
A broader range of tools utilized for managing user stories, testing, group management, client interaction
Make sure all claims are supported by the corresponding valid evidence and they are consistent.
All relevant supporting materials in appendices should be cross-referenced, cited as appropriate. (The marker will only read appendices if directed to do so in text body. Evidence should be hyperlinked to appendices and or GitHub)

All links throughout the documents should be hyperlinked and cross-referenced rather than providing the complete URL.
All tables, figures, diagrams, images should be numbered and captioned, and of high quality.
All documents status report, meeting minutes, scope statement…etc should be in a format that does not have to be downloaded to view e.g. screenshot, image, link …etc.

within Page limits, use of proper font size, submitted Acknowledgement of AI Use, and conducted Sparkplus
